question.worked_solution:
First, we multiply out the numerator and denominator of the sequence and get

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{(4n-1)(4n+1)}{n(7-16{n}^{2})}=\frac{16{n}^{2}-1}{7n-16{n}^{3}}.
$$

So to find the limit, we will need to compute

$$
{lim}_{n\to \infty }{a}_{n}={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{16{n}^{2}-1}{7n-16{n}^{3}}.
$$

The dominant term in the denominator is $-16{n}^{3},$ so we divide the numerator and the denominator by ${n}^{3}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{n\to \infty }{a}_{n} & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{16{n}^{2}-1}{7n-16{n}^{3}} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{16{n}^{2}}{{n}^{3}}-\frac{1}{{n}^{3}})}{(\frac{7n}{{n}^{3}}-\frac{16{n}^{3}}{{n}^{3}})} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{16}{n}-\frac{1}{{n}^{3}})}{(\frac{7}{{n}^{2}}-16)} \\  & =\frac{0-0}{0-16} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, the sequence converges and its limit is $0.$
